skill.name: reading-logseq-data
skill.description: Read data from Logseq DB graphs through the local HTTP API or Logseq CLI, including pages, blocks, properties, backlinks, and Datalog query results.
skill.summary: Read Logseq graph data with local API and CLI helpers.
skill.author: C0ntr0lledCha0s

security_audit.summary: Static command, network, environment, and reconnaissance matches were mostly false positives from documented local Logseq API and CLI access. Two semantic risks remain: bearer tokens can be sent to a configurable API URL, and CLI search fallback builds Datalog with unescaped search text.

remediation.issue: Bearer tokens are sent to any configured Logseq API URL.
remediation.suggestion: Default to localhost and require explicit user confirmation or allowlisting before sending Authorization headers to non-local hosts.

remediation.issue: Search fallback interpolates raw search text into Datalog.
remediation.suggestion: Use Datalog parameters for the search text or escape string literals before constructing the fallback query.

remediation.issue: CLI query parameters are accepted by the API but not passed through in _cli_query.
remediation.suggestion: Implement parameter passing for CLI queries or reject params in CLI mode so callers do not assume parameterization is active.

semantic_findings.title: Configurable API Endpoint Can Receive Bearer Token
semantic_findings.description: The client reads LOGSEQ_API_URL or .claude/logseq-expert/env.json and sends the bearer token to the configured URL. This supports custom deployments, but a malicious or mistaken configuration could disclose the Logseq API token to a non-local endpoint.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The code clearly combines configurable URLs with Authorization header transmission. The risk depends on user configuration, so confidence is high for the behavior but medium for exploitability.

semantic_findings.title: Unescaped Search Text in Datalog Fallback
semantic_findings.description: The CLI search fallback interpolates query_text directly into a Datalog string. A crafted search term containing quotes or Datalog syntax could alter the query or cause unexpected graph reads when CLI fallback is used.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The interpolation is direct and not parameterized. The impact is limited to local Logseq query behavior, but the injection pattern is concrete.

content.value_statement: Logseq users often need reliable access to pages, blocks, properties, and relationships without hand-writing every query. This skill gives Claude, Codex, and Claude Code structured helpers for reading local Logseq graph data.
actual_capabilities: Fetch Logseq pages and blocks by title or UUID.
Run Datalog queries against a Logseq graph.
Search graph content and limit returned results.
List pages, backlinks, and graph metadata.
Read page and block properties through HTTP API or CLI backends.
limitations: Requires a running Logseq HTTP API or installed Logseq CLI.
Needs a valid Logseq API token for HTTP operations.
Focuses on read operations and does not edit graph content.
Query results depend on the user graph schema and available properties.

use_cases.title: Inspect research notes
use_cases.description: Find pages, backlinks, and related blocks before summarizing a research topic.

use_cases.title: Build graph reports
use_cases.description: Run Datalog queries to list tasks, tagged items, ratings, or other structured Logseq data.

use_cases.title: Support local automation
use_cases.description: Use Claude Code to retrieve Logseq data through a reusable Python client in scripts.

prompt_templates.title: Fetch a page
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the Logseq reading skill to get the page named "Project Alpha" and summarize its blocks.

prompt_templates.title: Find backlinks
prompt_templates.prompt: Use Logseq to find backlinks to "Quarterly Planning" and group the results by source page.

prompt_templates.title: Query tagged items
prompt_templates.prompt: Run a Logseq Datalog query that finds all blocks tagged "Book" with a rating of 4 or higher.

prompt_templates.title: Audit task metadata
prompt_templates.prompt: Read my Logseq graph and list tasks with status "In Progress", including deadlines and parent pages when available.

output_examples.output: A concise page summary with properties, top-level blocks, and any missing page notice.

output_examples.input: List books rated at least 4 stars.
output_examples.output: A table-style summary of matching book titles, authors, and ratings when those properties exist.

best_practices: Keep the Logseq API bound to localhost unless remote access is required.
Use parameterized Datalog queries for user-supplied values.
Request only the fields needed to keep graph reads fast and private.
anti_patterns: Do not paste sensitive graph exports into prompts when local API access is enough.
Do not use broad pull-all queries for large graphs without a limit.
Do not configure API tokens for remote URLs you do not control.

faq.question: Does this skill modify my Logseq graph?
faq.answer: No. The documented operations focus on reading pages, blocks, properties, backlinks, and query results.

faq.question: What connection methods are supported?
faq.answer: It supports the local Logseq HTTP API and a CLI fallback when the Logseq CLI is available.

faq.question: Do I need an API token?
faq.answer: Yes for HTTP API calls. The token can come from parameters, environment variables, or local configuration.

faq.question: Can it run custom Datalog queries?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill includes examples and templates for Datalog queries against a Logseq DB graph.

faq.question: Is this useful for Markdown file graphs?
faq.answer: It is designed for Logseq DB graph access through API or CLI behavior. Results depend on Logseq support for the graph.

faq.question: Can Claude Code use the included Python client?
faq.answer: Yes. Claude Code can call the provided client library when local permissions allow file and command access.
